q: The Principal Chief Mechanical Engineer (PCME) is the head of which department of a zonal railway?
The Chief Workshop Engineer (CWE) is the ______ head of the department for workshops:
Direct control over the affairs of the workshops in a zonal railway is exercised by the:
Responsibility for budgetary control in a railway workshop rests with the:
On matters of workshop policy, the CWE issues instructions in consultation with the:

options.C: CME, the Principal Head of the Department

q: The officer who heads an individual railway workshop is generally known as the:
Which of the following statements about workshop administration is INCORRECT?

options.A: The PCME heads the Mechanical Department.
options.B: The CWE is the administrative head of the department for workshops.
options.C: Budgetary control in the workshop rests with the PCME.
options.D: The CWE consults the CME on workshop policy matters.

q: Assertion (A): The CWE issues policy instructions for workshops in consultation with the CME. Reason (R): The CME is the Principal Head of the Department.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

q: Production shops in a railway workshop are primarily concerned with:

options.D: Manufacture and repair of rolling stock and components

q: Maintenance sheds such as loco sheds and carriage/wagon depots are primarily concerned with:

options.A: Upkeep and maintenance of rolling stock in service

q: A unit manufactures wheel sets and bogies for supply to other railway units. In workshop terminology, this unit functions as a:
A diesel loco shed carries out scheduled maintenance of locomotives currently in service. This activity is best described as the work of a:
Which of the following best distinguishes a production shop from a maintenance shed?

options.A: Shops are physically larger than sheds.
options.B: Sheds work only during night hours.
options.C: Production shops manufacture and repair rolling stock and components; sheds maintain rolling stock in service.
options.D: There is no functional difference between them.

q: Which of the following statements about production shops and maintenance sheds is INCORRECT?

options.B: Maintenance sheds look after rolling stock in service.
options.C: Both serve the railway system of the zone.

q: Work orders in a railway workshop are processed by the:
The Production Control Organisation, which processes workshop work orders, functions under the authority of the:
Which of the following is NOT a typical objective of zonal railway workshops?

options.A: Repairs and maintenance of rolling stock

q: Assertion (A): Zonal workshops undertake repair works for rolling stock of other bodies. Reason (R): Workshops exist solely to serve their own division.

options.A: A is true, but R is false.
options.B: Both A and R are true.
options.C: A is false, but R is true.
options.D: Both A and R are false.

q: A newly posted officer is told he will exercise direct control over the affairs of the workshops of the zone. The post he holds is that of the:
Which of the following statements about the CME is correct?

options.A: The CME heads the Electrical Department.
options.B: The CME is the Principal Head of the Department whom the CWE consults on workshop policy.
options.C: The CME processes work orders in the workshop.
options.D: The CME is in charge of a single workshop.

q: The infrastructure of each shop and its planned outturn are fixed with reference to:

options.A: The demand and requirement of the railway system in the zone
options.B: The personal preference of the workshop manager

q: Shop outturn is assessed and matched to ensure that it is achieved to:

Match the authority with its workshop role: 1. CWE, 2. PCME, 3. CWM, 4. Production Control Organisation; (a) Head of Mechanical Department, (b) Processes work orders, (c) Administrative head of workshops department, (d) Heads an individual workshop.
A workshop officer issues a work order. The officer who heads the workshop, and under whose overall authority the work-order system operates, is the:
Which of the following is an INCORRECT pairing of authority and role?

options.A: CWE — budgetary control of the workshop
options.C: PCME — head of the Mechanical Department
options.D: Production Engineer — controls the Production Control Organisation

q: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense Account (WMS) is in the nature of a:
A workshop's WMS opens the year with a balance of Rs. 50 lakh (say). During the year it debits Rs. 200 lakh and credits Rs. 180 lakh (say). The closing balance is:
Which of the following is recorded on the debit side of the WMS account?

options.A: Expenditure on manufacture, i.e. labour, material and on-cost

q: Which of the following is recorded on the credit side of the WMS account?

options.D: Value of outturn of manufactured items

q: Which of the following statements about the WMS is INCORRECT?

options.A: It is a Capital Suspense Account.
options.B: It is closed to revenue at the end of every year.
options.C: Its debit side records manufacturing expenditure.
options.D: Its credit side records the value of outturn.

q: Assertion (A): WMS is described as a suspense account. Reason (R): Its opening and closing balances are carried forward from year to year.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

q: A work order completes manufacture of spares valued at Rs. 12 lakh (say). In the WMS account this is recorded on the:

options.D: Credit side as value of outturn

q: Labour wages of Rs. 5 lakh (say) are booked to manufacturing jobs during a month. In WMS this appears on the:
Which of the following is NOT debited to the WMS account?
The WMS account differs from an ordinary revenue expenditure head in that:

options.B: It is operated by the Stores Department.
options.C: It is a suspense account whose balances are carried forward and cleared by outturn.

q: The opening and closing balances of the WMS account are:
During a period, the value of outturn credited to WMS exceeds the manufacturing debits. The effect on the WMS balance is that it will:
Expenditure on manufacture booked through WMS is finally cleared when:

options.C: The manufactured items are valued as outturn and credited

q: Which of the following entries is INCORRECTLY stated for the WMS account?

options.A: Material consumed is credited to WMS.
options.B: Direct labour is debited to WMS.
options.D: Value of outturn is credited to WMS.

q: The WMS account is operated mainly to record:

options.D: Manufacturing and repair operations of the workshop

q: Assertion (A): On-cost is debited to the WMS account. Reason (R): On-cost forms part of the cost of manufacture.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

q: A workshop books labour Rs. 40 lakh, material Rs. 35 lakh and on-cost Rs. 15 lakh (say), and credits outturn of Rs. 90 lakh (say). The net change in the WMS balance is:
Which side of the WMS shows the cost incurred, and which shows the value realised?

options.A: Debit shows value realised; credit shows cost incurred.
options.C: Debit shows cost incurred; credit shows the value of outturn.
options.D: Neither side is distinguished in this manner.

q: Suspense accounts like WMS are used in workshop accounting because:

options.A: Cash is always in short supply.
options.C: Manufacture spans periods, and costs must be held until the outturn is valued.

q: Which of the following is NOT routed through the WMS account?

options.C: Stationery purchased for the workshop office

q: The balance under WMS at any point of time broadly represents:

options.B: Value of work-in-progress and manufactured items not yet cleared

q: Which of the following statements about WMS balances is INCORRECT?

options.A: They are carried forward from year to year.
options.B: They are increased by manufacturing debits.
options.C: They are reduced by outturn credits.
options.D: They are written off to revenue every year.

q: Assertion (A): WMS is a capital suspense account. Reason (R): It records manufacturing expenditure pending clearance by outturn credits.

options.A: A is true, but R is false.
options.B: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is false, but R is true.
options.D: Both A and R are false.

q: When manufactured spares are issued to the consuming department, the WMS account is:

options.B: Debited with the value of outturn
options.C: Credited with the value of outturn

q: Which of the following correctly states the accounting flow in WMS?

options.A: Debit: labour + material + on-cost; Credit: value of outturn; Balance: carried forward
options.B: Debit: value of outturn; Credit: labour + material
options.C: Both sides record only labour charges
options.D: Debits and credits are netted daily with no balances

q: Gross Credits of a workshop are Rs. 1,000 crore (say), all relating to Revenue works. The normal closing balance under WMS should be about:
Gross Credits of Rs. 800 crore (say) relate to Manufacturing works. The prescribed closing balance level under WMS is:
The prescribed closing-balance norm under WMS is higher for:

options.D: Both are kept at the same level

q: Which of the following statements about the WMS closing-balance norms is INCORRECT?

options.C: Revenue works: 6% and Manufacturing works: 3% of Gross Credits.
options.D: Balances should be kept at minimum or normal levels.

q: A key objective of the review of WMS is to ensure that closing balances are:

options.D: Kept at minimum or normal levels

q: The average hourly labour rates in a workshop have not been revised for several years. The WMS review flags this because:

options.B: Outdated rates distort the labour debits and the cost of manufacture
options.C: Rates once fixed can never be revised

q: Delays in revision of which of the following rates are specifically flagged in the review of WMS?

options.B: Average hourly rates and on-cost rates

q: Assertion (A): Outdated on-cost rates distort the WMS account. Reason (R): On-cost is levied as a predetermined percentage of direct labour.

options.A: A is true, but R is false.
options.B: A is false, but R is true.
options.C: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.D: Both A and R are false.

q: The managerial review of WMS checks, among other things:

options.B: Capacity utilization and deployment of resources

q: A review finds machines idle for long periods while some shops are overloaded with work. This finding relates to the review point on:
A specific aspect examined during the review of WMS is whether:

options.A: Materials and stores are drawn disproportionately compared to normal requirements

q: Spares are being manufactured far beyond the targets and are piling up in stock. The review objection is that manufacture of spares for stocking should be:

options.C: As per targets and should not result in accumulation in WMS

q: The review of WMS covers abnormal delay in closing work orders relating to:

options.C: Spares and components, and works done for outsiders

q: Which of the following is NOT a point of review under WMS?
Assertion (A): Closing balances under WMS should be kept at the minimum. Reason (R): Heavy uncleared balances indicate locked-up resources and inefficiency.

options.A: A is true, but R is false.
options.B: A is false, but R is true.
options.C: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.D: Both A and R are false.

q: A workshop's WMS closing balance stands at 12% of Gross Credits for Revenue works. The review will:

options.A: Flag it as abnormal, since the norm is 3%

q: The review of WMS is primarily aimed at:

options.D: Exercising financial and managerial control over workshop manufacturing operations

q: Actual indirect expenses have risen sharply, but the on-cost rate applied to jobs remains unchanged for years. The likely effect on WMS debits is:

options.A: Under-recovery: debits understate the true indirect cost

q: Timely revision of average hourly rates matters because labour debits to WMS are based on:

options.D: Those hourly rates, and stale rates misstate the cost of manufacture

q: Which of the following statements about the review of WMS is INCORRECT?

options.A: The review aims to increase closing balances.
options.B: The review checks timely revision of rates.
options.C: The review looks at capacity utilization.
options.D: The review covers delay in closing work orders.

q: Review of the progress of manufacture of spares for stocking ensures that it:

options.A: Is as per targets and does not result in accumulation

q: Work orders for jobs done for outside parties remain open years after completion. The review point attracted is:

options.B: Abnormal delay in closing work orders for works done for outsiders

q: Assertion (A): The WMS review examines deployment of men and machines. Reason (R): The review is limited to checking the arithmetic of the WMS account.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.B: A is true, but R is false.
options.C: A is false, but R is true.
options.D: Both A and R are false.

q: Which of the following best summarises the managerial review of WMS?

options.B: Checks on balances, rate revisions, capacity use, spares targets and work-order closure

q: A workshop revises its on-cost rate from 40% to 55% (say) after a review. Jobs executed after the revision will bear:
Direct cost in a workshop is a cost that:

options.C: Can be directly identified and traced to a specific job or work order
options.D: Is never recorded in the books

q: Wages of a fitter who works solely on Job No. 101 during the month are:

options.D: Direct labour cost of Job No. 101

q: Cotton waste used generally across all jobs in a shop is classified as:

options.D: Indirect material forming part of shop on-cost

q: In workshop cost accounting, indirect expenses are commonly termed:
Which of the following statements about direct and indirect costs is INCORRECT?

options.A: Direct costs are traceable to a job.
options.B: Indirect costs are apportioned through on-cost rates.
options.C: Wages of a worker engaged on a specific job are an indirect cost.
options.D: Cotton waste for general shop use is an indirect cost.

q: A fixed cost is a cost which:

options.A: Remains constant in total within the capacity, regardless of output
options.B: Varies directly with every unit produced

q: The monthly rent of the workshop building, say Rs. 1 lakh, does not change with the level of production. It is a:
Power consumed by machines rises and falls with production. Such power cost is a:
Machine maintenance cost has a fixed monthly inspection charge plus a usage-based repair component. It is a:
Which of the following statements about fixed and variable costs is INCORRECT?

options.A: Total fixed cost is constant within capacity.
options.B: Total fixed cost rises in direct proportion to output.
options.C: Total variable cost rises with output.
options.D: Semi-variable costs have both fixed and variable elements.

q: On-costs in workshop accounting are best described as:

options.D: Indirect expenses levied as a predetermined percentage

q: Assertion (A): Indirect costs cannot be traced to a single job. Reason (R): They are apportioned to jobs through predetermined on-cost rates.

options.A: A is true, but R is false.
options.B: A is false, but R is true.
options.C: Both A and R are false.
options.D: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

q: A job has direct labour Rs. 10,000 (say), direct material Rs. 6,000 (say), and on-cost at 50% of direct labour (say). The total cost of the job is:
Prime cost of a workshop job consists of:

options.C: Direct material, direct labour and direct expenses

q: The difference between the prime cost and the total cost of a job is mainly accounted for by:
Which of the following is an example of indirect labour?

options.B: Welder on a specific work order
options.C: Shop supervisor overseeing all jobs in the shop

q: Lubricating oil used for all machines in a shop is classified as:
Semi-variable costs are also known as:
Which of the following is NOT an indirect cost?

options.D: Steel plates issued specifically to Job 205

q: Assertion (A): Depreciation of the workshop building is treated as a fixed cost. Reason (R): It does not vary with the level of production in the short run.

options.A: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.B: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.C: A is true, but R is false.
options.D: A is false, but R is true.

q: A shop's on-cost rate is 60% of direct wages (say). A job with direct wages of Rs. 5,000 (say) will bear on-cost of:
Cost accounting in workshops primarily helps the management to:

options.D: Ascertain the cost of each job and control costs

q: For a job executed for an outside party, the most relevant cost for fixing the charge is the:

options.C: Total cost including on-cost, so that full cost is recovered

q: Which of the following statements on cost concepts is INCORRECT?

options.B: On-costs are charged at actuals with no predetermined rate.
options.D: Indirect costs are apportioned, not traced.

q: The correct sequence of cost build-up for a workshop job is:

options.A: Total cost, then prime cost, then on-cost
options.B: On-cost, then prime cost, then total cost
options.C: Prime cost, then total cost, then on-cost
